stem: In a family, P is the father of Q. Q is the brother of R. R is the mother of S. S is the brother of T. U is the wife of P. T is married, and T's spouse is a man. Treating every marriage in this family as between a man and a woman, how is T related to P?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Grandson has the right generation but the wrong gender. T's spouse is a man and all marriages here are man-woman, so T is a woman; the grandchild of P who is female is a granddaughter, not a grandson.

Q brother of R with P father of Q and U his wife makes R a daughter of P. R is the mother of S, and S is the brother of T, so T is also a child of R, hence a grandchild of P. T's spouse is a man, and marriages here are man-woman, so T is a woman. A female grandchild of P is P's granddaughter.
Daughter places T one generation below P, but T is a child of R, who is herself a child of P. That is two generations below P, a grandchild, not a daughter.
Niece would make T the child of P's sibling. T descends through P's own daughter R, so T is in P's direct line two generations down, a grandchild, not a niece.

explanation: Build the tree top down. P and his wife U have children; Q is their son and Q is the brother of R, so R is their daughter. R is the mother of S, and S is the brother of T, so T is another child of R. That makes T a grandchild of P, two generations below him. T's gender is never stated by a relation word, so infer it: T is married to a man, and the puzzle fixes marriages as between a man and a woman, so T is a woman. A female grandchild of P is his granddaughter.

explanation_sections.punchline: T's spouse is a man, so under man-woman marriage T is female; being two generations below P, T is his granddaughter.
explanation_sections.approach: Fix the generations first using the sibling and parent links: Q and R are children of P and U; S and T are children of R; so T sits two levels below P, a grandchild. Then resolve the only open gender: no premise names T as son or daughter or brother or sister, but T's spouse is a man and all marriages are man-woman, which forces T female. Combine grandchild plus female to get granddaughter, and check the chain T to R to P is exactly two steps.
explanation_sections.lesson: When no relation word gives a person's gender, infer it from a spouse or sibling clue before naming the final gendered relation.
explanation_sections.timing: About 145 seconds. Fastest elimination is option (3) Daughter: T descends through R, who is already P's daughter, so T is plainly a generation too low to be P's daughter.
